The Calydonian Boar. A massive, supernatural wild boar sent by the goddess Artemis to devastate the kingdom of Calydon as punishment for a king's impiety. King Oeneus had failed to honor her with proper sacrifices, and Artemis's response was to unleash this terrible beast upon his land. The boar's hide was impenetrable to normal weapons, making it nearly impossible to kill through conventional means. Its size was enormous—described as being as large as a bull or larger—with tusks capable of goring warriors and their horses alike.

The hunt that followed required the assembly of the greatest heroes of the era. Jason came, and Theseus, and Heracles, and many others—a gathering that would later serve as a precursor to the expedition for the Golden Fleece. Among these legendary warriors was Atalanta, a swift huntress and warrior who proved herself their equal. She was the first to draw blood from the beast, striking it with her spear before any of the male heroes could land meaningful blows. Meleager, the king's son, ultimately delivered the killing blow to the weakened beast, but the honor belonged to Atalanta. The boar's death sparked fierce conflict over the trophy pelt. Atalanta's role became a point of contention, revealing the deep prejudices of the age. Despite its supernatural origin and destructive power, the boar was described more as an instrument of divine will than as a conscious monster.
